summary: Old Chang Moi Road (Chang Moi Kao) is a historic commercial street in Chiang Mai’s Chang Moi district, known for rattan and basketware shops alongside cafés and newer creative businesses. It works best as a casual walk linking Tha Phae Gate, the neighborhood’s lanes and Warorot Market, rather than as a single attraction with fixed hours.
whyGo: See working basketry and rattan storefronts in an old trading neighborhood, with independent cafés and converted shophouses nearby.
Combine a low-key street walk with Warorot Market, the Ping River area or an Old City visit on foot.
bestFor: Travelers interested in everyday commercial streets, craft shopping, cafés and street photography.
A flexible 1–2 hour walk that can be extended into Warorot Market and the riverfront.
skipIf: You want a major landmark, curated museum experience or guaranteed lineup of open shops.
You need a smooth, step-free pedestrian route throughout; sidewalks and shop thresholds are not formally documented.
duration: Allow about 1 hour for a relaxed walk and browsing; 1–2 hours with a café stop or a longer wander to Warorot. These are planning estimates.
cost: Walking the public street is free. Shopping, café and food costs depend on the business and item; no reliable current price list was found. Ask the price before buying and carry some cash.
hours: The road is public and accessible at all times, but the experience depends on individual shops and cafés. A Chiang Mai resident’s 2026 neighborhood guide recommends mornings, when more workshops are working; confirm any specific business directly before making it your anchor.
bestTime: Go in the morning for cooler walking and a better chance of seeing workshops open. Avoid assuming that every rattan shop opens daily or keeps the same hours.
gettingThere: Start near Tha Phae Gate and walk east through Chang Moi’s lanes toward Warorot Market; a current local guide estimates about 5 minutes from the gate to Chang Moi and 5–10 minutes onward to Warorot, depending on the exact start and pace. From elsewhere in Chiang Mai, take a red songthaew, taxi or ride-hail to Tha Phae Gate or Chang Moi and continue on foot. Traffic and year-end congestion can affect vehicle times.
booking: No booking or admission is needed for the street. Reserve or check directly with a café only if you have a particular stop in mind; the local business mix and hours can change.
accessibility: No formal accessibility information for the street was found. Expect ordinary city sidewalks, traffic crossings and possible uneven surfaces or merchandise outside shopfronts; interiors may have raised thresholds or limited room. A step-free continuous route is not confirmed.
practicalTips: Use both names when navigating: Old Chang Moi Road is also called Chang Moi Kao Road; the wider district and main road are often called Chang Moi Road.
Look for working rattan and basketware shops, then explore nearby lanes and cafés; shops displaying goods outside are businesses, so ask before photographing people or interiors.
Support shops by browsing respectfully and buying a small item if you take photos of a storefront; keep walkways and entrances clear.
Pair the walk with Warorot Market for food and shopping, but check market hours separately because it has its own schedule.
decemberNotes: December mornings are a sensible time for a walk, but no December 2026 street event, special hours or holiday schedule was confirmed. Shops may set their own holiday hours and year-end traffic may slow rides; check a chosen business shortly before visiting.
uncertainties: No official street-wide opening hours, current directory of rattan shops, or confirmed December 2026 holiday schedule was found; local guidance describes the neighborhood broadly and individual businesses may change.
The local guide’s walking times are neighborhood estimates, not measured directions to a specific storefront.
Accessibility conditions vary by block and shop, and no continuous step-free route was documented.
